Hannah —

We started seeing systematic latency spikes and 500 errors on calls routed to our dedicated pool starting ~07:50 PDT this morning. Per our contract we have reserved capacity for 1,200 qps sustained for the peak window; our monitoring shows sustained token-level queueing and timeouts (samples attached).

Key metrics:
- 07:50–08:10 PDT: median latency jumped from 80ms -> 420ms
- Error rate (5xx) climbed to 3.8% over 20 minutes
- Queue depth on the dedicated pool reported by your telemetry: avg 420 items

This is materially impacting our ability to process end-of-day reconciliation jobs. We flagged this to support at 07:56 and opened incident #MF-2916; we need an immediate mitigation (burst add or fallback) and a written explanation of why our reserved throughput appears short.

Attached: consolidated logs + sample request IDs. Please escalate to engineering and leadership — our CPO is on standby and legal is asking about SLA credits if this is a breach.

Thanks,
Matt Rivera
Head of Infrastructure, MicroFin

Hannah / team —

Preliminary triage notes after looking at the logs:
- The dedicated pool serving MicroFin shows a persistent KV-cache miss storm between 07:45–08:05 that increased per-request memory pressure; kernel telemetry indicates we hit a GPU memory compaction path more frequently than baseline. This causes GC-like stalls and queue piling.
- We see correlated increased allocation churn on a single host (gpu-12b-03) — likely a noisy neighbor (multi-tenant placement) combined with an unexpected model kernel path change rolled in last week.

Immediate mitigations I'm triggering now:
1) Requesting a 30-minute burst allocation (+25% headroom) for MicroFin while we shift their 15% of highest-latency traffic to an adjacent dedicated variant. (Priyom, please authorize if procurement/commit impacts are acceptable.)
2) Pinning MicroFin's serving set to the prior kernel path to avoid the GC path until we can patch.
3) Isolating gpu-12b-03 from new placements and draining it as a precaution.

I will follow with a short RCA and timeline for a permanent fix.

-David
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
